zh.summary: 用操作流程回答使用者如何完成任務，再用架構回答軟體由什麼組成、資料如何移動及誰負責控制。
objectives: 分開User Flow的操作順序與架構的結構關係。
指出瀏覽器、Python程序、程序內規則及下載檔的不同位置。
為架構假設標記依據、邊界與仍需驗證的問題。

readingGuide.goal: 分開User Flow的操作順序與架構的結構關係。
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md、wireframe-notes.md及工作坊reference/；可只閱讀與畫圖，不需啟動程式。
readingGuide.route: 先看情境與原理，再比較例子，最後擴寫 architecture.md 並用檢核題自查。
readingGuide.output: architecture.md能與User Flow互相對照，又清楚分開操作順序與軟體結構。

sections.heading: 操作與結構各回答什麼問題？
paragraphs: 這一課最重要的觀念是：使用者怎麼操作軟體，跟軟體內部怎麼運作，是兩件不同的事。

- User Flow（使用者流程）：描述一個人怎麼完成任務。
- System Architecture（系統架構）：描述有哪些軟體組件、各自負責什麼、如何互相溝通，以及資料存放在哪裡。
本課的目標是把使用者流程與系統架構分別畫清楚，並讓兩者互相對照。

sections.heading: 一、先用餐廳來理解
paragraphs: 想像你今天開了一間餐廳。
客人來吃飯，他的流程可能是：

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜User Flow：客人怎麼完成用餐
blocks.description: 箭頭表示這個簡化案例的操作順序。餐廳內部的系統分工留給下一張圖。

items.title: 入座
items.body: 客人找到座位。

items.title: 點餐
items.body: 選擇並送出餐點。

items.title: 等待
items.body: 等候餐點送達。

items.title: 用餐
items.body: 享用餐點。

items.title: 結帳
items.body: 完成付款。

paragraphs: 這是一個完整的 User Flow。
但是，如果你是餐廳老闆，光知道客人會「點餐、吃飯、結帳」，能不能開好餐廳？
不能。你還需要知道：

- 點餐資料由服務生記錄，還是送到電子點餐系統？
- 廚房如何知道要做哪些菜？
- 庫存系統怎麼知道食材用掉多少？
- 結帳時是誰計算金額？
- 如果刷卡機故障，怎麼處理？
這些問題開始涉及餐廳內部的組織、設施與資訊系統。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜餐廳資訊系統如何運作（假設範例）
blocks.description: 箭頭是資訊傳遞關係：點餐平板→訂單管理系統；訂單管理系統分別傳給廚房、庫存與結帳系統。下方三者是平行接收者，沒有彼此先後關係。

items.title: 點餐平板
items.body: 送出訂單 → 訂單管理系統

items.title: 訂單管理系統
items.body: 接收訂單，分送三類資訊。

items.title: 廚房顯示器
items.body: 訂單管理系統 → 出餐資訊

items.title: 庫存系統
items.body: 訂單管理系統 → 用量

items.title: 結帳系統
items.body: 訂單管理系統 → 金額

paragraphs: 概念示意：方框是系統或設備，箭頭是資訊傳遞關係；不是客人的操作順序。
客人的操作流程完全相同，餐廳內部卻可能有非常不同的架構。
小吃店可以用紙本菜單、口頭通知廚房；大型連鎖餐廳可能有點餐平板、POS 系統、中央資料庫與支付服務。
外面看起來做一樣的事情，裡面可能是完全不同的系統。

sections.heading: 二、用一張表建立完整觀念
paragraphs: 先分清各自要回答的問題，再選擇圖中的元素與驗證方法。

blocks.caption: 表｜二、用一張表建立完整觀念
rows: 工程師、架構師、維運人員
程序、服務、儲存、通訊與責任
組件是否正確協作，且符合品質與安全要求？

paragraphs: 兩者不是二選一，而是彼此補充。

sections.heading: 三、回到真正的軟體開發：同一個功能，怎麼畫兩種圖？
paragraphs: 教材使用的是一套「收件資料檢核系統」。假設工作人員必須輸入資料，系統檢查是否缺漏，通過教學欄位完整性規則後才能下載報告；這不代表資料真實、正式受理或業務核准。

blocks.heading: 第一張圖：User Flow
paragraphs: 先追蹤正常操作，再看缺漏分支如何回到檢查。

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜收件資料檢核的 User Flow
blocks.description: 填寫→檢查→完整性判斷。否：顯示缺漏→補填或修正→回到檢查；是：預覽→下載 JSON。這是操作條件與回復流程，不是軟體架構。修改輸入會使舊結果失效，匯出前再驗證。

items.title: 填寫收件資料
items.body: 輸入三個必要教學欄位。

items.title: 按下檢查
items.body: 檢查目前輸入。

items.title: 資料完整嗎？
items.body: 依教學完整性規則分成是／否。

items.title: 否：顯示缺漏欄位
items.body: 指出需要補填或修正的地方。

items.title: 補填或修正
items.body: → 回到「按下檢查」，使用更新的輸入。

items.title: 是：預覽結果
items.body: 檢視目前輸入對應的檢查結果。

items.title: 下載 JSON 報告
items.body: 下載前再驗證；完整不代表正式受理。

paragraphs: 這張圖可以回答「少填資料怎麼辦？」、「可以重新檢查嗎？」、「什麼時候能匯出？」
但你還不知道，究竟是誰在檢查資料。

blocks.heading: 第二張圖：System Architecture
paragraphs: 教材參考專案實際採用 Streamlit 和 Python，並不是完整的 React、API、資料庫三層式系統。可以用下圖表示主要結構：

blocks.caption: 圖 4｜Streamlit 程序與資料位置
blocks.description: 使用者→瀏覽器；瀏覽器↔Python／Streamlit程序為Streamlit通訊（WebSocket）。rules.py與Session State都位於同一Python程序內；雙向符號表示呼叫／結果或讀寫，不表示獨立服務。JSON下載到使用者裝置。主機分組不代表已驗證的安全信任邊界。

items.title: 使用者
items.body: 操作瀏覽器。

items.title: 瀏覽器：操作介面
items.body: 輸入與結果顯示；↔ Python／Streamlit程序。

items.title: Python／Streamlit 程序
items.body: 執行驗證與報告產生。

items.title: rules.py：驗證規則
items.body: 程序內直接呼叫／回傳結果。

items.title: Session State：工作階段記憶體
items.body: 程序內暫存輸入與已檢查快照；讀／寫。

items.title: 使用者裝置上的 JSON 檔案
items.body: 瀏覽器 → 下載；與伺服器記憶體分開管理。

paragraphs: 這張圖開始回答不同問題：

- Browser（瀏覽器）：負責呈現畫面，讓使用者輸入與查看結果。
- Python Process（Python 程序）：負責執行程式、檢查資料、產生報告。
- rules.py（規則模組）：放置資料驗證邏輯，由 Python 程序直接呼叫。
- Session State（工作階段狀態）：暫時保存該工作階段需要的資料。
- JSON（資料格式）：用結構化方式表達檢查結果，供下載或其他程式使用。
特別注意：教材沒有實作獨立的 REST API、持久資料庫，也沒有呼叫外部 AI 模型來檢查欄位。不能因為這些技術常見，就自行把它們畫進既有架構。
Streamlit 官方文件也確認，它有瀏覽器端與 Python 伺服器端，並使用 WebSocket 維持互動與工作階段通訊。因此即使你在自己的電腦執行，概念上仍存在 Client–Server（用戶端與伺服器）分工。

blocks.heading: 把兩張圖連起來
paragraphs: 用同一個操作逐列對照處理位置。

blocks.caption: 表｜三、回到真正的軟體開發：同一個功能，怎麼畫兩種圖？
headers: 系統裡實際需要發生的事情
rows: 瀏覽器收集輸入，應用程式管理狀態
系統產生驗證結果，介面顯示提示
使用更新後的輸入重新驗證
程式產生 JSON，瀏覽器提供下載

paragraphs: 每個有意義的操作，都應該能追蹤到負責處理它的軟體部分。

sections.heading: 四、理解幾個經常混淆的技術觀念
paragraphs: 判讀架構時，請分別核對檔案、執行程序與資料生命週期，並依使用規模檢查責任。

blocks.heading: 1. 程式檔案不等於獨立服務
paragraphs: 假設有以下兩個 Python 檔案：

blocks.heading: rules.py
paragraphs: 同目錄的獨立練習檔；兩者在一個程序執行。

blocks.heading: app.py
paragraphs: 同目錄的獨立練習檔；兩者在一個程序執行。
blocks.code:
# app.py（與 rules.py 放在同一目錄）
from rules import validate
result = validate({"name": "Alice"})
print(result)

paragraphs: 在 Python 3 環境把上例分成 rules.py 與 app.py，執行 python3 app.py，預期印出 True。完成後可刪除這兩個練習檔及 __pycache__；不要刪除工作坊原始程式。這個最小例子只檢查 name 的真假值，不等於工作坊三欄位的完整驗證規則。
這通常只是同一個 Python 程序中的模組呼叫，不代表有兩台伺服器。
要稱為獨立服務，通常需要有自己的執行邊界，可能透過 HTTP、訊息佇列等方式與其他服務溝通。

blocks.heading: 2. 沒有資料庫，不等於沒有資料
paragraphs: 想像你在網站填寫資料，但沒有按儲存。
資料可能仍然存在瀏覽器或伺服器的記憶體中。你下載的檔案也可能長期留在電腦裡。
因此，架構設計必須問的不只是「有沒有資料庫」，還包括「資料在哪裡、存多久、誰能存取、什麼事件會使資料消失」。

blocks.heading: 3. 本機執行，不等於已經安全
paragraphs: 假設一個程式原本只有一個人使用，現在要給十名員工使用。
介面可能完全不用修改，但架構需要重新思考登入驗證、權限、不同使用者的資料隔離、同時執行的資源使用，以及伺服器失敗後如何復原。
換句話說，User Flow 不變，並不代表 System Architecture 不需要改變。

sections.heading: 五、不同產業的實際運用
paragraphs: 下列情境用來練習分辨操作問題與結構問題，並非特定機構的實際架構。

blocks.caption: 表｜五、不同產業的實際運用
rows: 病患如何掛號、查詢、取消？
掛號系統怎麼連接醫院資料庫？
誰計算信用評分？資料送去哪裡？
客戶如何查詢包裹進度？
掃碼資料如何傳送、保存與更新？
使用者如何上傳檔案並取得摘要？
文件解析、模型推論與儲存在哪裡執行？
消費者如何下單及退款？
如何協調訂單、庫存、金流與退款？

paragraphs: 同一個 User Flow 可能有許多種技術實作。選擇架構時，要根據資料量、使用人數、安全需求、成本與維運能力，而不是只根據介面看起來有多少功能。

sections.heading: 六、下一步：C4 Model 是什麼？
paragraphs: C4 Model 是一種用不同縮放層級說明軟體架構的方法，可以把它想成軟體的 Google Maps。

blocks.caption: 圖 5｜C4 架構模型的四個層級
blocks.description: 向下箭頭表示逐層放大結構，不表示執行順序。依問題選擇有幫助的層級，不必每次畫完四層。Container不一定是Docker容器。

items.title: C1 · System Context
items.body: 誰使用系統？與哪些外部系統合作？

items.title: C2 · Container
items.body: 有哪些應用程式、服務及資料儲存？

items.title: C3 · Component
items.body: 單一應用程式內有哪些功能組件？

items.title: C4 · Code
items.body: 組件內部有哪些類別、函式與程式碼？

paragraphs: C4 中的 Container 指應用程式或資料儲存等軟體單位，不一定是 Docker Container。而 C4 架構圖主要描述結構；如果要描述某一次操作發生的精確呼叫順序，可以額外使用 Sequence Diagram（循序圖）。
延伸閱讀請見本節的 C4 Model 官方來源。

sections.heading: 七、實際應用：如何要求 AI 幫你設計？
paragraphs: 以後當你要使用 AI Coding Agent 開發軟體時，可以使用這樣的順序：

1. 先定義使用者要完成什麼任務，以及成功條件。
2. 畫出 User Flow，涵蓋正常操作、判斷分支與錯誤復原。
3. 根據功能、資料與非功能需求提出 System Architecture。
4. 把每個重要操作對應到實際處理的模組與資料位置。
5. 區分「已實作」、「設計提案」與「待確認」，再檢查安全邊界。
對既有專案尤其重要：不要讓 AI 憑想像畫一張漂亮的架構圖，而要讓它檢查程式碼、設定與部署環境，說明每個架構元素的證據。

sections.heading: 八、理解檢核
paragraphs: 試試看以下三題，不必先查答案。
三題理解檢核列於本文下方，各題可展開參考解析；不記錄學員作答或判定學習完成。
User Flow 告訴我們人如何完成工作；System Architecture 告訴我們軟體如何承擔這份工作。兩種圖互相對照，才能從「看起來能用」走向「知道它如何運作、如何驗證、如何維護」。

exercise.environment: problem.md、wireframe-notes.md及工作坊reference/；可只閱讀與畫圖，不需啟動程式。
steps: 將既有User Flow寫在左欄，右欄列出每步涉及的瀏覽器、程序、規則與資料位置。
核對reference/app.py及rules.py，將未見依據的外部服務標為待確認或移除。
在architecture.md寫下目前結構及至少一項共用版仍需重新設計的責任。
exercise.expected: architecture.md能與User Flow互相對照，又清楚分開操作順序與軟體結構。
exercise.check: 不把畫面步驟當容器，不虛構資料庫或REST API；能指出下載檔與記憶體資料不同。
exercise.cleanup: 保留合成標記、依據與待確認事項；不複製真實業務架構或秘密。

en.summary: Use a user flow to explain task completion, then architecture to explain software structure, data movement and control responsibilities.
objectives: Separate User Flow action order from architectural structure.
Locate the browser, Python process, in-process rules and downloaded files separately.
Label architectural assumptions with evidence, boundaries and unresolved questions.

readingGuide.goal: Separate User Flow action order from architectural structure.
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md, wireframe-notes.md and workshop reference/ files. Reading and drawing are sufficient; no program startup is required.
readingGuide.route: Read the situation and principles, compare examples, then expand architecture.md and use the checks to review your understanding.
readingGuide.output: architecture.md connected to the User Flow while clearly separating action order from software structure.

sections.heading: What do actions and structure each explain?
paragraphs: How people operate software and how the software works internally answer different questions.

- User Flow describes how a person completes a task.
- System Architecture describes the software units, their responsibilities and communication, and where data is kept.
The aim is to draw both views clearly and connect them to each other.

sections.heading: 1. Start with a restaurant
paragraphs: Imagine that you run a restaurant.
A customer might follow this dining process:

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | User Flow: how a customer completes a meal
blocks.description: Arrows show the action order in this simplified example. Internal system responsibilities belong to the next diagram.

items.title: Take a seat
items.body: The customer finds a seat.

items.title: Order
items.body: Choose and submit dishes.

items.title: Wait
items.body: Wait for the meal to arrive.

items.title: Eat
items.body: Enjoy the meal.

items.title: Pay
items.body: Complete payment.

paragraphs: This is a complete User Flow for this simplified dining scenario.
As the owner, can you run the restaurant merely by knowing that customers order, eat and pay?
You also need to answer these questions:

- Does a waiter record orders, or do they enter an electronic ordering system?
- How does the kitchen know which dishes to prepare?
- How does inventory management know how much food was used?
- Who calculates the bill?
- What happens if the card terminal fails?
These questions involve the restaurant's internal organization, equipment and information systems.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | A restaurant information system (hypothetical)
blocks.description: Arrows show information relationships: ordering tablet → order management; order management separately sends information to kitchen, inventory and billing systems. The three receivers are parallel, not successive steps.

items.title: Ordering tablet
items.body: Order → order management

items.title: Order management
items.body: Receive orders and distribute three kinds of information.

items.title: Kitchen display
items.body: Order management → preparation details

items.title: Inventory system
items.body: Order management → usage

items.title: Billing system
items.body: Order management → amount

paragraphs: This is a conceptual example: boxes are systems or devices, and arrows show information relationships rather than the customer's action sequence.
The customer's actions can stay the same while the restaurant's internal architecture differs substantially.
A small eatery may use paper menus and spoken kitchen orders. A chain may use ordering tablets, a POS system, a central database and payment services.
Similar visible tasks can therefore be supported by very different systems internally.

sections.heading: 2. Compare the two views
paragraphs: Identify the question each view answers before selecting its elements and verification methods.

blocks.caption: Table | 2. Compare the two views
rows: How does the user complete the task?
How does the system support it?
Processes, services, stores, communication and responsibilities
How can a user return after a mistake?
How does the program recover from failure?
Can the user complete the actions?
Do units cooperate correctly and satisfy quality and security requirements?

paragraphs: The views complement each other; both can describe the same product.

sections.heading: 3. Draw two views of the same software feature
paragraphs: The course uses an intake-data completeness checker. A staff member enters data, the system checks for missing fields, and a report becomes downloadable after the teaching completeness rules pass. This establishes neither factual truth nor official intake or business approval.

blocks.heading: First view: User Flow
paragraphs: Trace the normal actions, then follow the missing-information branch back to Check.

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | User Flow for the intake completeness checker
blocks.description: Enter → check → completeness decision. No: show omissions → correct → return to Check. Yes: preview → download JSON. These are actions and recovery conditions, not software architecture. Editing invalidates old results; export revalidates.

items.title: Enter intake data
items.body: Enter the three required teaching fields.

items.title: Press Check
items.body: Check the current input.

items.title: Is the data complete?
items.body: Branch on the teaching completeness rules.

items.title: No: show missing fields
items.body: Identify information to supply or correct.

items.title: Supply or correct data
items.body: → Return to Press Check with updated input.

items.title: Yes: preview results
items.body: Inspect results for the current input.

items.title: Download JSON report
items.body: Revalidate before download; completeness is not official intake.

paragraphs: This view answers what happens when information is missing, whether the user can check again, and when export is available.
It still leaves open which software actually checks the data.

blocks.heading: Second view: System Architecture
paragraphs: The reference project uses Streamlit and Python. It does not implement a full React, custom API and database three-tier system. Its main structure is:

blocks.caption: Figure 4 | Streamlit processes and data locations
blocks.description: User → browser; browser ↔ Python/Streamlit process uses Streamlit communication (WebSocket). rules.py and Session State are inside the same Python process. Bidirectional symbols mean calls/results or reads/writes, not independent services. JSON downloads to the user device. Host grouping does not establish a security trust boundary.

items.title: User
items.body: Operates the browser.

items.title: Browser: user interface
items.body: Input and result display; ↔ Python/Streamlit process.

items.title: Python/Streamlit process
items.body: Run validation and generate reports.

items.title: rules.py: validation rules
items.body: Direct in-process calls and returned results.

items.title: Session State: session memory
items.body: Input and checked snapshots held inside the process; read/write.

items.title: JSON file on the user device
items.body: Browser → download; managed separately from server memory.

paragraphs: This view answers another set of questions:

- Browser: presents the interface for entry and viewing results.
- Python process: runs the program, checks data and produces the report.
- rules.py: contains validation logic called directly by the Python process.
- Session State: temporarily holds data needed by that session.
- JSON: represents check results in a structured format for download or use by other programs.

The reference implements no separate REST API or persistent database, and calls no external AI model to check the fields. Familiar technologies should appear in the current architecture only when they are actually present.

Streamlit's official documentation describes the browser client and Python server, with WebSockets maintaining interactive session communication. The client-server division still exists when both run on your own computer.

blocks.heading: Connect the two views
paragraphs: Compare each action with its processing location.

blocks.caption: Table | 3. Draw two views of the same software feature
headers: What must happen inside the system
rows: The browser gathers input and the application manages state
The system produces validation results and the interface displays guidance
The program produces JSON and the browser offers the download

paragraphs: Each meaningful action should be traceable to the software responsible for handling it.

sections.heading: 4. Resolve commonly confused technical ideas
paragraphs: Inspect files, running processes and data lifecycles separately, and review responsibilities against the intended usage scale.

blocks.heading: 1. A program file is not an independent service
paragraphs: Suppose you have these two Python files:

blocks.heading: rules.py
paragraphs: Separate practice file in the same directory; both run in one process.

blocks.heading: app.py
paragraphs: Separate practice file in the same directory; both run in one process.
blocks.code:
# app.py（與 rules.py 放在同一目錄）
from rules import validate
result = validate({"name": "Alice"})
print(result)

paragraphs: In Python 3, save these as rules.py and app.py in the same directory, then run python3 app.py. The expected output is True. Afterwards, delete only these practice files and their __pycache__, retaining the original workshop program. This minimal example checks the truth value of name; it does not reproduce the workshop's complete three-field validation rules.
This is normally an in-process module call, not evidence of two servers.
An independent service normally has its own execution boundary and may communicate with other services through HTTP, a message queue or another mechanism.

blocks.heading: 2. No database does not mean no data
paragraphs: Imagine entering information on a website without pressing Save.
The data may still exist in browser or server memory. A downloaded file may remain on the computer for a long time.
Architecture must therefore ask where data exists, how long it remains, who can access it and which events remove it, in addition to asking whether there is a database.

blocks.heading: 3. Running locally does not establish security
paragraphs: Suppose a program used by one person will now serve ten employees.
Its interface may remain unchanged, while authentication, authorization, separation of users' data, concurrent resource use and recovery after server failure all need reconsideration.
An unchanged User Flow can therefore require a changed System Architecture.

sections.heading: 5. Apply the distinction across industries
paragraphs: These scenarios help distinguish action questions from structure questions; they do not describe the actual architecture of any particular organization.

blocks.caption: Table | 5. Apply the distinction across industries
rows: How do patients book, look up and cancel appointments?
How does the booking system connect to hospital databases?
How does a customer apply for a loan?
Who calculates credit scores, and where is data sent?
How does a customer track a parcel?
How are scan records transmitted, stored and updated?
How does a user upload a file and obtain a summary?
Where do document parsing, model inference and storage run?
How do customers order and request refunds?
How are orders, inventory, payments and refunds coordinated?

paragraphs: Many implementations can support the same User Flow. Select an architecture using data volume, user count, security requirements, cost and operational capacity, rather than only the apparent number of interface features.

sections.heading: 6. Next: what is the C4 model?
paragraphs: The C4 model explains software architecture at different zoom levels, much like zooming through a software map.

blocks.caption: Figure 5 | Four levels of the C4 model
blocks.description: Downward arrows mean zooming into structure, not execution order. Use the levels that help answer the question; all four are not always necessary. A container is not necessarily a Docker container.

items.title: C1 · System Context
items.body: Who uses the system? Which external systems cooperate with it?

items.title: C2 · Container
items.body: Which applications, services and data stores exist?

items.title: C3 · Component
items.body: Which functional components exist within an application?

items.title: C4 · Code
items.body: Which classes, functions and code exist within a component?

paragraphs: A C4 container is an application or data store, not necessarily a Docker container. C4 architecture diagrams mainly describe structure. Add a sequence diagram when you need the precise order of calls in a particular operation.
For further reading, follow the official C4 model sources linked in this section.

sections.heading: 7. Ask AI to help design the system
paragraphs: When developing software with an AI coding agent, use this order:

1. Define the user's task and success conditions.
2. Draw the User Flow, including normal actions, decisions and recovery.
3. Propose System Architecture based on functions, data and non-functional requirements.
4. Map each important action to the modules and data locations that handle it.
5. Distinguish implemented behavior, design proposals and unknowns, then inspect security boundaries.

For an existing project, ask the agent to inspect code, configuration and deployment evidence and justify every architectural element. An attractive imagined diagram cannot establish the actual architecture.

sections.heading: 8. Check your understanding
paragraphs: Try the three questions without consulting the answers first.
The three checks appear below, each with an expandable reference explanation. They do not record learner answers or establish learning completion.

User Flow explains how people complete work; System Architecture explains how software supports that work. Cross-checking the two helps you explain how the product operates, how to verify it and how to maintain it.

exercise.environment: problem.md, wireframe-notes.md and workshop reference/ files. Reading and drawing are sufficient; no program startup is required.
steps: Put the User Flow in one column and the browser, process, rules and data locations for each step in another.
Inspect reference/app.py and rules.py. Mark unsupported external services as unknown or remove them.
Write current structure and at least one shared-version responsibility needing redesign in architecture.md.
exercise.expected: architecture.md connected to the User Flow while clearly separating action order from software structure.
exercise.check: Do not treat screens as containers or invent databases/REST APIs. Distinguish downloads from memory data.
exercise.cleanup: Keep synthetic labels, evidence and unknowns. Copy no actual business architecture or secrets.

zh.prompt: 一個購物網站的流程是「選商品 → 加入購物車 → 結帳」。你想知道付款資料有沒有傳到第三方公司，應該看哪一種圖？
rationales: 操作流程說明人如何完成任務，沒有完整描述資料接收者。
架構圖應標示外部系統、傳送的資料與責任邊界，可追蹤付款資料去向。
畫面只能顯示可見操作，無法證明後端資料流。

en.prompt: A shopping flow is Select products → Add to cart → Checkout. Which diagram helps determine whether payment data reaches a third party?
rationales: The action sequence does not fully identify data recipients.
Architecture should identify external systems, transferred data and responsibilities so payment data can be traced.
Screens cannot establish backend data flows.

zh.prompt: AI 幫你建立了 app.py、rules.py、export.py 三個檔案。是否可以直接宣稱系統包含三個獨立服務？
options: 可以，一個檔案就是一個服務
不可以，要確認實際執行與通訊邊界
rationales: 檔案拆分可以只是同一程序內的模組。
需查核程序啟動方式與通訊；三個檔案不足以判定三個服務。
程式語言本身不決定服務數量。

en.prompt: AI creates app.py, rules.py and export.py. Can you immediately claim that the system has three independent services?
options: Yes, each file is a service
No; inspect actual execution and communication boundaries
Yes, as long as it uses Python
rationales: Files can be modules inside one process.
Inspect process startup and communication; three files do not establish three services.
The language does not determine service count.

zh.prompt: 原本單人使用的程式要改成 100 人共同使用，畫面與操作完全相同。最應優先確認的是？
options: 使用者權限、資料隔離、併發與維運能力
是否可以增加更多動畫
rationales: 外觀一致無法確認共用版的資料及容量責任。
使用規模改變，需要驗證授權、隔離、資源使用與失敗復原。
動畫不回答多人共用帶來的架構問題。

en.prompt: A single-user program will serve 100 people with the same screens and actions. What should you prioritize?
options: Permissions, data isolation, concurrency and operations
rationales: Visual consistency does not establish shared-data or capacity responsibilities.
A change in scale requires checking authorization, isolation, resource use and recovery.
Animation does not answer shared-use architecture questions.
